new_findings: X1 is NOT nonmonotonic as hypothesized — all effects are monotonic (concave/saturating). High initial sensitivity was misleading.
Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3 (all other inputs have exactly zero effect). Linear model: Y3 ≈ 0.52*X1 + 0.67*X3 - 0.015.
Y4 depends ONLY on X2 (+0.18), X4 (+0.16), and X6 (-0.07). X1 has a tiny effect (+0.058 range). X3 and X5 have zero effect.
X2 has ZERO effect on Y3 despite initial correlation of -0.485 — entirely spurious.
X5 ONLY affects Y1, and saturates above ~0.55 (goes from -0.058 to 0.244 between X5=0.1-0.55, then barely changes to 0.244 at X5=1.0).
X4 is a surprisingly strong driver of Y1 (range=0.390, largest single-input effect on Y1) while also decreasing Y2 and increasing Y4 — a triple win.
X6 increases Y1 (range=0.269) but also increases Y2 (+0.139) and decreases Y4 (-0.074), creating trade-off tensions.
Y1 has the lowest R² (0.77) in linear regression with all inputs, suggesting possible nonlinearities or interactions.
surprises: X1 was predicted nonmonotonic but is actually monotonically increasing for all outputs — the high sensitivity estimate from 6 initial points was misleading.
X3 was predicted flat for Y1 but actually increases it substantially (range=0.236).
X2 was predicted to decrease Y3 (correlation -0.485) but has exactly zero effect — the correlation was entirely spurious from covariance with other varying inputs.
X6 was predicted flat for Y1 but increases it substantially (range=0.269) — initial correlation was low (0.03) but the true causal effect is meaningful.
X4 has the largest single-input effect on Y1 (range=0.390), which was not evident from the initial 6-point correlations.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Test for interactions, especially affecting Y1 (R²=0.77 suggests missing nonlinearities). Priority: (1) X2*X4 interaction on Y1 and Y4 since both are strong drivers, (2) X5 saturation — test if X5's saturation point depends on other inputs, (3) X1*X3 interaction on Y3 since both drive it. Then explore the Pareto front to understand the Y1-Y2-Y4 trade-off mediated by X2 and X6.

new_findings: Y3 is MULTIPLICATIVE: Y3 = f(X1)*g(X3). Verified by constant ratios across 3x3 grid (within 0.5%). This explains the poor linear R²=0.73 and the calibration error.
X2*X4 interaction on Y1 is the strongest found (std=0.114): at X2=1,X4=1 Y1=0.844 vs additive prediction ~0.628. X4's effect on Y1 is 7x larger when X2=1.0 vs X2=0.1.
X2*X6 and X4*X6 are ANTAGONISTIC on Y1 — X6's positive effect on Y1 diminishes when X2 or X4 are already high (substitutes, not complements).
X5 saturation confirmed at two operating points: at X4=0.55, X5 saturates at ~0.55; at X4=1.0, X5 saturates at ~0.7. The saturation threshold SHIFTS with X4.
X4's effect on Y2 may REVERSE at extreme operating points: gradient switches from -0.58 at low values to +0.25 at high values, suggesting a nonmonotonic regime.
Y4 gradients are near-zero when X2 and X4 are both low (all <0.007), suggesting multiplicative-like structure where the effects of X2, X4, X6 compound.
X6 reverses its effect on Y1 at the extreme high operating point: gradient goes from +0.44 at low-X2/X4 corner to -0.03 at high-X2/X4 corner.
X1*X3 interaction on Y3 is confirmed (std=0.100) — the multiplicative structure means their joint effect exceeds any additive model prediction.
surprises: The X2*X4 synergy on Y1 is FAR stronger than expected: Y1 at (X2=1,X4=1)=0.844 vs 0.433 or 0.435 for each alone — nearly double the additive prediction.
X6's effect REVERSES on Y1 depending on operating point — beneficial at low X2/X4 but negligible/negative at high X2/X4. The full-range gradient comparison revealed this.
dY1/dX2 ranges from 0.007 (essentially zero at low X2/X4) to 1.28 (dominant at high values) — a 180x change. X2's contribution to Y1 is extremely position-dependent.
X5 saturation threshold shifts with X4 (from ~0.55 to ~0.7), indicating X5 interacts with the rest of the system despite appearing independent in individual sweeps.
Y2's response to X4 appears to reverse at extreme operating points (gradient -0.58 at low values, +0.25 at high values), creating a regime-dependent trade-off.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Budget is exhausted. For optimization: (1) Set X1 and X3 high (0.8-1.0) to satisfy Y3≥0.4 and improve Y1,Y2. (2) X4 high improves Y1,Y4 and Y2 at moderate levels, but watch for Y2 reversal at extremes. (3) X5≥0.7 to ensure saturation benefit. (4) The main Pareto trade-off is X2 vs X6: high X2 with low X6 maximizes Y4 and Y1 (via X2*X4 synergy) while limiting Y2 damage; high X6 with low X2 improves Y2 but sacrifices Y4 and some Y1. (5) Test candidate Pareto points: [1,1,1,1,0.7,0.1], [1,0.5,1,1,0.7,0.1], [1,0.3,1,1,0.7,0.3].
